title: Discovery call - check-in bottlenecks
body: Danielle walked through intake at their three hospitals. Avg check-in at the main campus ED-adjacent registration is 14-18 min; peaks at 25+ on Monday mornings. Front desk re-keys demographics and insurance from paper forms into the EHR, so roughly 6% of claims kick back for registration errors. She owns the patient experience scores and they dropped two quarters in a row. Wants mobile pre-registration plus kiosk/tablet at the desk. Mentioned another vendor is already piloting at one outpatient clinic. Next step: technical session with Priya on EHR integration.

title: Recap + intro to Clinical Applications
body: Sent Danielle recap of discovery: 3 sites, ~1,100 registrations/day combined, target cut check-in time in half. Asked her to loop in Priya Venkataraman for the integration review. She replied same day and cc'd Priya.

title: Technical deep-dive - EHR integration
body: 90 min with Priya and two of her analysts. Covered HL7 ADT feeds, FHIR patient/coverage resources, insurance card OCR, and write-back of consent forms to the chart. Her concerns: interface engine capacity, who owns the interface build, and SSO with their identity provider. We confirmed our team builds and tests the interfaces; she estimates 6-8 weeks of her team's partial time. She's neutral - said the competitor pilot hasn't touched the EHR yet, it's standalone. Wants security questionnaire and BAA template.

title: Proposal sent - Digital Patient Intake
body: Sent proposal to Danielle, cc Priya: 3 hospitals, mobile pre-reg, desk tablets, EHR integration, 3-year term. $185K year one including implementation. Attached security questionnaire responses and BAA. Asked for 30 min to walk through with finance.

title: Pricing call with CFO
body: Gregory joined with Danielle. He pushed hard on price - says the competitor pilot is running at roughly 40% less per site and wants to know why he shouldn't just expand that. Our answer: their pilot has no EHR write-back, so staff still re-key data; savings come from the integration. He wasn't convinced, wants hard numbers on FTE hours and denial reduction, not vendor case studies. Also asked about phasing payments by site. Skeptical but didn't say no.

title: Deal strategy after CFO call
body: Risk: CFO anchoring on competitor pilot pricing. Plan: build ROI off Acme's own numbers (1,100 regs/day, ~6% registration denials, front-desk overtime). Consider phased go-live by hospital to spread year-one cost. Need Priya to confirm in writing the competitor has no EHR integration roadmap for their pilot.

title: Champion request - ROI summary for CFO
body: Danielle emailed asking for a one-page ROI summary she can bring to Gregory before their budget review. Wants: front-desk hours saved, denial reduction in dollars, payback period, and a side-by-side vs. the pilot. She said contract is otherwise ready to go once finance signs off.

title: Send ROI summary to Danielle for CFO review
body: One-pager: FTE hours saved at 3 sites, registration denial reduction ($), payback period, phased payment option, comparison vs. competitor pilot (no EHR write-back). Get finance to validate denial assumptions before sending.

title: ROI review with CFO and VP Patient Ops
body: Tentatively booked 30 min with Gregory and Danielle to walk through ROI summary and answer pricing questions ahead of contract signature.

title: Inbound demo request after intake webinar
body: Rachel Lindqvist submitted a demo request after attending our 'Cutting Check-In Time in Half' webinar. Form notes: 11 clinics, paper intake packets, front desk re-keys insurance info into the EHR. Asked about tablet and text-to-patient options. Routed to me; good ICP fit for the mid-size network segment.

title: Re: Your Brightwell demo request
body: Thanked Rachel for attending the webinar, sent the 3-minute patient-side walkthrough video and offered intro call times. Asked her to bring rough numbers on daily visit volume and average check-in time if she has them.

title: Intro/discovery call with Rachel (Ops)
body: Good call. Pains: average check-in runs 12-14 min at busiest sites, waiting room backs up Monday mornings. Front desk staff spend ~2 hrs/day scanning and re-keying paper forms. Two clinics (East Washington and Fitchburg) had overtime spikes last quarter. Rachel wants to pilot at those two of the eleven clinics first, then expand if numbers hold. Concerns: EHR integration effort and older patient adoption of text links. Budget would need COO sign-off; she thinks low $40Ks for a pilot is workable. Next step: get COO Thomas Brennecke in a meeting.

title: Pilot outline + EHR integration summary
body: Sent Rachel a one-page pilot outline for the two clinics: 90-day pilot, kiosk + SMS pre-registration, insurance card capture, success metrics (check-in time, forms re-keyed per day, front desk overtime). Attached EHR integration summary and an accessibility note on in-clinic tablet fallback for patients who don't use text.

title: Re: Pilot outline - COO meeting
body: Rachel replied that she shared the outline with Thomas and he agreed to a 45-min meeting next week. He wants to see cost per clinic at full rollout, not just the pilot price, and how long before front desk staff are trained. She'll pull baseline check-in data from the two pilot sites before the meeting.

title: Build 11-clinic rollout pricing and ROI model
body: Prepare pilot price ($42K) plus full 11-clinic rollout pricing. ROI based on Rachel's numbers: ~2 hrs/day re-keying per site, overtime at two pilot clinics. Include training timeline (target under one week per site).

title: Prep call with Rachel before COO meeting
body: Quick 15-min sync to review baseline data and confirm what Thomas cares about most (cost vs. staff time). Confirm who else might join from IT.

title: Pilot review with COO Thomas Brennecke
body: Agenda: Rachel's baseline check-in data, 2-clinic pilot scope and success metrics, full rollout cost per clinic, EHR integration and training plan. Goal: COO agreement on pilot scope and path to paperwork.
